questions.text: A debugger breakpoint resolves to an address but has zero hits. What does resolution alone establish?

options.A: The function executed successfully for the current input.
options.B: The function is unreachable for every possible input.
options.C: The breakpoint has a location; execution at that location has not been observed.
options.D: The compiler removed every instruction from the function.

questions.explanation: Resolution associates a breakpoint with code. It does not prove a hit, a completed run, or global unreachability; hit counts and run context are separate evidence.

questions.text: A stack-style core preserves a label pointer, but the pointed-to string lives in an executable segment omitted from the core. How should you report the string?

options.A: Unavailable in this capture; the displayed empty string does not establish its value.
options.B: Confirmed empty, because the debugger displayed quotation marks with no text.
options.C: Corrupted, because a valid pointer must refer to bytes inside the stack core.
options.D: Confirmed unchanged, because pointer equality proves all pointed-to bytes.

questions.explanation: The pointer is captured but the pointee bytes are absent. Core coverage limits what can be observed, so the display cannot establish an empty or unchanged string.

questions.text: rollup checks refuted count first, then confirmed count, otherwise not-observed. A claim has four confirmed records and one refuted record. Which verdict does it receive?

options.A: confirmed, because four records outvote one.
options.C: An exception, because mixed verdicts are forbidden.
options.D: refuted, because any refutation takes precedence.

questions.explanation: The first branch tests whether the refuted count is nonzero, so one refutation determines the verdict regardless of the confirmed count.
